recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If the work group wants a new substantive design for multiple XHTML Narrative fragments or translated Narrative extensions, handle that as a new issue rather than reopening FHIR-15759.
issue_request: FHIR-15759 was a Published FHIR-core Change Request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3, asking for multi-language support for Narrative translation. The approved resolution was to document the use of XHTML lang in the language page and include the W3C i18n HTML language-declarations link, rather than adding a translated XHTML extension or a repeated Narrative.div element.
initial_application: The issue was first applied as a ballot note in source/narrative.html by d9f49dd27615ab53608acbdc1746e8dcdb3f3263, corresponding to the Jira comment for svn revision 13555. The final application was 1764ff51c3db67afa6aa35d51c6f04532073a097, corresponding to svn revision 14164, which added language-page guidance and converted the narrative ballot note into current multi-language narrative prose.
additional_context: source/languages.html is an active specification page through source/hierarchy.xml and contains the requested XHTML lang guidance plus the W3C language-declarations link. source/narrative.html is active through source/fhir.ini type-page mappings for narrative/xhtml and carries parallel guidance. The originating Zulip thread explains why the change request was filed, and bounded Jira/Confluence checks found no later related decision that changes the published resolution.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source change was needed because the current source already satisfies the final issue resolution; further edits would only restate or polish existing guidance rather than correct a semantic defect.
